question: Given that agriculture is one of Europe’s key assets, is the Commission considering an initiative to align interest rates for agricultural loans across Europe, providing for: 1.
low-interest loans for investment, refinancing and working capital, facilities that must be on a par throughout Europe;
the setting of interest rates for a period of at least 3 years;
low interest rates that must come as a package with no fees, such as analysis fees or arrangement fees?
answer: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) provides a wide range of support measures for farmers, including financial instruments (FIs) such as loans, guarantees and equity. In the new period, 12 Member States have programmed in their CAP Strategic Plans (CSPs) EUR 1 billion total public support as loan or guarantee funds (1).

However, the CAP does not provide for a possibility of harmonised interest rate subsidies across Member States as it is applied in shared management and FI support is given through the financial market, the conditions of which are different in each Member State.

Further, through the use of FIs supported by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) farmers can obtain investment loans with lower interest rates and/or working capital finance. Member States may also use grants in the form of interest rate subsidies to support private loans taken by farmers. The Commission is assisting the EAFRD managing authorities in this field through fi-compass (2).

Member States have the freedom to design the conditions of their FIs under the CAP in the way that best reflects the market needs. Member States can also supplement the CAP FI support by granting state aid to farmers.

In this case, lower interest rate loans for farmers introduced by Member States, or similar forms of support, would most likely constitute state aid in the meaning of Article 107(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. If a Member State wishes to grant such aid, it can design a state aid scheme and set the conditions/modalities (e.g.

duration and administrative formalities), which will have to be notified to and approved by the Commission, or which could be implemented without prior notification and approval if compliant with the relevant provisions of the Agricultural Block Exemption Regulation (3).

Member States need to perform an ex-ante assessment to see which FI is the one in need and what should be its underlining conditions. For the use of FIs supported by the EAFRD in the period 2014-2022, see the situation report by end 2022 available at: https://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/funding/financialinstruments_en https://www.fi-compass.

eu/funds/eafrd Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/2472 of 14 December 2022 declaring certain categories of aid in the agricultural and forestry sectors and in rural areas compatible with the internal market in application of Articles107 and 108 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, OJ L 327 of 21.12.2022, p.1.
